messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: venn diagram?
parts:
Java doesn't run well on Spark and Glimmer. This is because we lock down processes to 2GB of virtual memory using "ulimit -v" (in response to a few users repeatedly consuming dozens of GB of RAM, whether on purpose or accidentally). By default, Java attempts to reserve lots and lots of virtual memory (without actually allocating it) so it crashes.

http://superuser.com/questions/472587/why-does-limiting-my-virtual-memory-to-512mb-with-ulimit-v-crash-the-jvm

Try calling this BEFORE using any rJava functions, to tell Java to limit the heap to 512MB:
.jinit(parameters="-Xmx512m")

On Thursday, September 26, 2013 1:50:13 PM UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
Java doesn't run well on Spark and Glimmer. This is because we lock down processes to 2GB of virtual memory using "ulimit -v" (in response to a few users repeatedly consuming dozens of GB of RAM, whether on purpose or accidentally). By default, Java attempts to reserve lots and lots of virtual memory (without actually allocating it) so it crashes.

http://superuser.com/questions/472587/why-does-limiting-my-virtual-memory-to-512mb-with-ulimit-v-crash-the-jvm

Try calling this BEFORE using any rJava functions, to tell Java to limit the heap to 512MB:
.jinit(parameters="-Xmx512m")
